items.title: Chapo calls for cooperation to protect Africa’s strategic minerals
items.summary: Maputo, 25 Oct (AIM) – Mozambican President Daniel Chapo has called for stronger cooperation among African countries and international organizations to protect the continent’s natural resources amid growing international competition for strategic minerals, natural gas and oil. Speaking at the 12th Tana Forum in Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, on Saturday, Chapo argued that geopolitical rivalries and the global energy transition require African countries to coordinate their efforts to ensure that natural resources contribute to the development of the countries that possess them. The Head of State drew attention to the timing of the discovery of major natural gas reserves in Mozambique’s northern province of Cabo Delgado in 2016 and the emergence of terrorism in the region in 2017, suggesting that the proximity of the two events was too striking to ignore. “We discovered gas reserves in 2016 in Cabo Delgado, and around the same time, terrorism appeared in 2017.

items.title: Government plans to create 500,000 jobs under PNDC
items.summary: Maputo, 25 Oct (AIM) – The Mozambican Government plans to create 500,000 jobs by formalizing 10,000 cooperatives and integrating 1.5 million informal economy operators into the formal sector. The plan is part of the 20-year National Cooperative Development Programme (PNDC). According to Economy Minister Basílio Muhate, speaking at the launch of PNDC 2026–2046, in Maputo, the initiative seeks to organize small-scale producers and other economic operators into cooperatives to strengthen their bargaining power, improve access to financing and facilitate the marketing of locally produced goods. “More than eight out of every ten Mozambicans work in the informal economy. Vendors, fishermen, carpenters, artisans and farmers generate income and support families but face difficulties because they operate individually. These are not complaints from people who do not want to work.

items.summary: Health officials are investigating whether Ebola patients in Kenya and Nigeria crossed paths at Uganda's main airport as conflicting accounts cloud the source of one infection The first confirmed Ebola patients in Kenya and Nigeria may have crossed paths at Uganda's Entebbe International Airport, according to African health officials, as new information from Switzerland contradicts Uganda's account of the Nigerian patient's travel history Uganda , a country reporting no active Ebola infections, has become a focus of investigations into cases thousands of kilometers apart Uganda insists that it has no confirmed active cases of the deadly virus .

items.title: 'I cannot teach you integrity': How employee theft is hurting small businesses in Africa
items.summary: Kenyan food creator That Girl Boina shut her waxing studio due to employee theft When popular Kenyan food creator That Girl Boina took a two-week holiday to Europe, she expected to relax. A week into the trip, an Instagram direct message exposed a problem that would ultimately lead to the closure of her business "I was at your studio, I liked everything. The only problem was that I was asked to send money to a different number. It wasn't the number on the wall," a customer wrote to her Boina had opened Waxaholic Studio, a waxing and hydrafacial parlour in Nairobi's central business district, on 1 September 2024. A year later, she had hired a receptionist and two specialists and felt confident enough to take a two-week holiday, her first international trip of the year "I trusted them. It's two rooms and a reception - how do you mess that up?" she recalls thinking "It never occurred to me that maybe I was getting clients and someone else was stealing from me," she tells the BBC The discovery prompted Boina to examine the business more closely.

items.title: Venezuelan opposition leader María Machado returns after months in exile
items.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has returned home to a fraught political landscape after over 10 months in exile "I am here. With you," Machado wrote on X on Sunday Her ally, former presidential candidate Edmundo González, confirmed the news minutes later, writing: "I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear María Corina, is on Venezuelan soil." items.title: Protein shakes for teenagers: Good or bad idea?
items.summary: Protein products are marketed as a way of building muscle and losing weight — and they're very popular with young people. They also claim to promote healthy growth in children. Is this true? How much protein is healthy? You can take it as a powdered drink, or in a snack bar. Puddings and certain breads are also promoted as "sources of protein," and protein-enriched products like Kindershake and Teen Balance are specifically designed to appeal to a young people — and it appears to be working In a representative survey of almost 1,000 parents by the University of Michigan in 2024, just under half said their children, who were aged 13 to 17, had consumed protein products over the previous year.

items.title: Early reports suggest record high turnout in Serbia elections

items.title: Gunmen kill at least 10 villagers and loot shops in north-east Nigeria
